comment: Every numeric identifier namespace this repository allocates for itself.
Read by tools/registers/check-ids.mjs. Each namespace names the register
that defines its identifiers, the anchored pattern that constitutes a
definition, who repairs a collision, and every identifier that is burned.
A namespace with no `why` is a fault, not a default: a reader who cannot
tell why an identifier is burned cannot tell whether reissuing it is safe.
NOT IN HERE, deliberately. docs/standards/lessons.md allocates L-A and L-E
and is a vendored copy of an HQ standard, so neither a collision nor a
burn in it is repairable in this repository at all; HQ allocates those
with its own tools/check-queue-ids.sh. docs/agents/incidents.md keys on
INC-<date>-<slug>, which is content-derived rather than allocated, so two
runs cannot race for the same one.
`repair` is a locus from tools/gates/verdict-shape.mjs. `owner` means a
seat must not touch it: an accepted ADR is the owner's decision record and
renumbering one rewrites what other files already cite.

namespaces.name: ADR
namespaces.why: Architecture decisions, numbered in date order per the convention the file follows everywhere else. Cited by docs/agents/org-chart.md, docs/backlog.md, skills/running-an-outcome-record-trial/SKILL.md and three workflow files.

namespaces.name: PWC
namespaces.why: Changes a seat designed and cannot apply, queued for the chair or the owner. The unscoped namespace is the security seat's since the 2026-10-04 split; the other seats took their own prefixes.

burned.why: Redaction gate. Applied by the chair 2026-09-24 and the entry deleted per the file's own rule, so the identifier resolves to nothing while docs/security/ still cites it.
Product-plan redaction. Applied 2026-09-24, entry deleted, same as PWC-1.
Trial README redaction. Applied 2026-09-24, entry deleted, same as PWC-1.
Repository description and topics. Applied 2026-09-24, entry deleted, same as PWC-1.

Meant two different changes in two unmerged pull requests at once (#46 and #74), which is the collision this gate exists for; the engineer seat's copy became PWC-ENG-1 on 2026-10-05 and docs/security/audit-2026-10-04.md still cites the bare number twice.
Renamed in place to PWC-EXO-4 when the identifiers became seat-scoped on 2026-10-04. docs/agents/learning-log.md cites the old number twice.

namespaces.name: PWC-ENG
namespaces.why: The engineer seat's own queue, split out of the unscoped namespace on 2026-10-05 after PWC-7 collided.

namespaces.name: PWC-EXO
namespaces.why: The ExO seat's own queue, split out of the unscoped namespace on 2026-10-04. PWC-EXO-1 through 4 were renamed in place from PWC-7 through PWC-10.
